pages.name: Carel ir33 / ir33+
pages.recognize: Compact panel display; the code shows in place of the temperature with a bell icon.
pages.title: What Do Carel ir33 Alarm Codes Mean? E0, HI, LO, dor, CHt
pages.h1: What do Carel ir33 / ir33+ alarm codes mean?
pages.meta: Every Carel ir33 / ir33+ alarm code: probe faults E0-E3, HI/LO, IA/dA, dor, cht/CHt, LP, Pd, EE/EF, HA/HF. What it means, what to check, when to call.
pages.short_answer: Short answer: an ir33 announces a fault by showing its code on the display; when several alarms are active they are shown in sequence. rE and E0–E3 are probe faults, HI/LO are temperature alarms, IA, dA and dor come from contacts wired to the controller, cht/CHt watch the condenser, LP, Pd and AtS are refrigerant-side pressure and pump-down alarms, EE/EF are memory errors that shut the controller down, and HA/HF are HACCP temperature records. Carel's full table is below, with a detailed section for every code people most often see.
pages.display_html:
Many ir33 alarms switch on the alarm relay and buzzer — but not all of them. Probe faults E0–E3, the condenser pre-alarm cht, the clock fault Etc, the memory errors EE/EF and the HACCP records HA/HF stay silent, so a quiet controller can still be showing a fault. The table's relay column shows which is which.

Press Prg/mute to silence the buzzer. That clears nothing: the code and the alarm relay stay active until the reading is back inside its threshold. Alarms with manual reset are cleared by pressing Prg/mute and UP together for more than 5 seconds — do that only after fixing the cause. Status messages are not faults: dEF means a defrost is running; Ed1/Ed2 means a defrost on evaporator 1 or 2 ended on time instead of temperature.

table_rows.meaning: Probe S4 fault — the same fault as E2, on the fourth probe input
Autostart in pump down
Type HF HACCP alarm — high temperature after a power failure (blackout); logged with date, time and duration
A unit (1 to 6) in a networked group of controllers has an alarm
Defrost on evaporator 2 ended by timeout
Start defrost call
End defrost call
Continuous cycle running
Start continuous cycle call
End continuous cycle call
HACCP menu accessed
Manual-reset alarms, HACCP alarms or temperature monitoring have been reset
Controller switched on / switched off
Probe not enabled

diagnosis: Write down every code before touching anything. If several alarms are active the display shows them in sequence. Read the box temperature on an independent thermometer too.
Sort the code. Probe (rE, E0–E3) · temperature (HI, LO, AFr) · inputs (IA, dA, dor) · condenser (cht, CHt) · refrigerant side (LP, Pd, AtS) · controller (EE, EF, Etc) · HACCP record (HA, HF).

Probe faults mean the box is running blind. With rE or E0 the compressor runs on the fixed duty cycle set by parameter c4 instead of on temperature, so the box keeps cooling but can drift warm or freeze product. Check the probe cable and its terminal connection (NTC probes have no polarity), then compare the displayed reading against your thermometer.

Temperature alarms are delayed on purpose. HI and LO trigger only after the temperature has stayed past the AH/AL threshold for the delay set in parameter Ad, so by the time HI shows the box has been warm for a while. They reset automatically once the temperature is back inside the threshold.

IA and dA come from whatever is wired to the digital input. What the compressor does during them is set by parameter A6 (0 = compressor always off, 100 = always on). Find out which device is connected to that input before suspecting the controller.

Fix, then reset. AFr (frost protection), CHt (high condenser temperature) and LP (low pressure) switch the compressor off. AFr, CHt, HA and HF need the manual reset — Prg/mute + UP for more than 5 seconds — and clearing CHt without cleaning the condenser just brings it back.

EE and EF stop everything. The memory errors shut the controller down — compressor, defrost and fans off. One power cycle is a fair test; if the code returns, the controller needs reprogramming or replacement by a technician.
Read the HACCP record. The HACCP menu shows the year, month, day, hour, minute and duration of the last three HA/HF events — the record a health inspector will ask for.

parts.part: Control probe S1 (NTC or PTC thermistor)
parts.note: A probe that drifts without failing outright can produce false HI/LO alarms.

parts.part: Defrost probe S2 on the evaporator
parts.note: When a defrost can't reach its end temperature it ends on time and Ed1/Ed2 is shown.

parts.part: Probes S3 / S4 (condenser or auxiliary, as configured)
Door switch on the digital input
Device wired to the external-alarm input

parts.note: Refrigerant-side work for an EPA 608-certified technician.

parts.part: The controller itself (parameter memory, real-time clock)

pages.name: Carel PJ Easy (PJEZ)
pages.recognize: Small Carel thermostat; E0/E1/E2, dOr and cht/CHt alternate with the temperature.
pages.title: What Do Carel PJ Easy (PJEZ) Codes Mean? E0, dOr, CHt & More
pages.h1: What do Carel PJ Easy (PJEZ) alarm codes mean?
pages.meta: Every Carel PJ Easy (PJEZ) alarm code: E0/E1/E2 probe errors, HI/LO, dOr, IA, cht/CHt, Ed, EE/EF, EtC. What it means, what to check, when to call a tech.
pages.short_answer: Short answer: when a PJ Easy alarms, the code flashes alternating with the temperature and — where fitted and enabled — the buzzer and alarm relay switch on. E0, E1 and E2 are probe errors (control, defrost, condenser/product), HI/LO temperature alarms, dOr the door, IA an external alarm, cht/CHt a dirty condenser, Ed a defrost that ended on time, EE/EF parameter errors and EtC the clock. Every alarm clears itself once its cause is gone except CHt, which needs a manual reset.
pages.display_html: Press SET to mute the buzzer; the code and the alarm relay only go off when the cause has been resolved. To reset CHt, switch the controller off and on with the UP button (hold it 3 seconds) or disconnect the power — after cleaning the condenser. dF on the display just means a defrost is running.

table_rows.meaning: Maintenance request (easy split only): the maintenance interval set in parameter HMP has passed; cleared by setting HMr = 1

diagnosis: Note the code and the real temperature. Read the box on a separate thermometer before you change anything.
Mute, don't clear. SET silences the buzzer; the code and relay stay on until the cause is fixed.

E0, E1, E2 are probe 1 (control), probe 2 (defrost) and probe 3 (condenser/product). PJ Easy and easy compact models take Carel NTC probes (10 kΩ at 25 °C) or PTC probes (985 Ω at 25 °C), depending on the model's order code; easy split models use NTC or high-temperature NTC probes (50 kΩ). A replacement probe must match what the controller is set up for. Thermistor probes have no polarity.
dOr is the door switch. If the pre-alarm times A7 and d8 are both zero the alarm is immediate. It resets when the door is closed, or when the controller is switched off with UP for 3 seconds.
Ed means a defrost ended on time, not temperature. It clears after the next defrost that ends correctly — look at the coil for ice before then.
cht, then CHt. cht is the dirty-condenser pre-alarm; CHt is the full alarm and the only one that needs a manual reset. Clean the condenser coil with the power off, then reset.
EtC clears by setting the time. EE/EF are parameter-memory errors — a technician job if a power cycle doesn't clear them.

parts.part: Probe 1 — control / room probe (NTC or PTC)
Probe 2 — defrost probe on the evaporator

pages.name: Danfoss ERC 211 / 213 / 214
pages.recognize: Danfoss ERC 21X display; E27/E29/E30 sensor errors and A01–A99 alarms.
pages.title: What Do Danfoss ERC 211/213/214 Codes Mean? E29, A01, A80 & More
pages.h1: What do Danfoss ERC 211, 213 and 214 alarm codes mean?
pages.meta: All 12 Danfoss ERC 211/213/214 codes: sensor errors E27, E29, E30 and alarms A01, A02, A04, A15, A45, A61, A80, A99, AA1. Meaning, checks and reset.
pages.short_answer: Short answer: the ERC 21X series uses two kinds of code. E-codes mean a sensor is defective or its connection is lost — E29 the air sensor (Sair), E27 the evaporator/defrost sensor (S5), E30 the condenser sensor (Sc). A-codes are alarm conditions: temperature (A01/A02), supply voltage (A99/AA1), condenser (A61/A80), door (A04), an external input (A15) and standby (A45). Danfoss's table has twelve codes, and all twelve have a full section below.
pages.display_html: One key does double duty: a short press scrolls, but pressing and holding it for about 3 seconds switches the main switch on or off — an easy way to put a box into A45 standby without meaning to. Holding it while powering up triggers a factory reset, so don't do that while troubleshooting.
diagnosis: Rule out A45 first. A45 means control was stopped by the r12 main switch — someone switched it off, not something broken. Switch it back on and watch the box pull down.

E-codes are a sensor or its wiring. E29 (air, Sair), E27 (evaporator, S5) and E30 (condenser, Sc) mean the sensor is defective or its electrical connection is lost. Check the plug and cable before replacing the sensor.

Match the sensor type. The ERC accepts NTC 5 kΩ (EKS 211), NTC 10 kΩ (EKS 221), PTC 990 Ω (EKS 111) or Pt1000 (AKS 11, 12, 21) sensors, selected in parameter o06. A replacement that doesn't match the setting reads wrong from day one.

Condenser: A61 warns, A80 locks out. A61 means condenser temperature is too high — check the airflow. A80 is the condenser-blocked alarm and needs a manual reset: set the r12 main switch off and on again, or power the controller down — after cleaning the coil, or it comes straight back.
A99 and AA1 are about the building's supply voltage — too high or too low — and exist to protect the compressor. If they repeat, the fix is electrical, not refrigeration.
A04 and A15 come from the digital input. A04 is the door open too long; A15 is an external alarm on DI1, and what DI1 does is set by parameter o02 — so check what's wired there.

pages.name: Danfoss EKC 202 / AK-CC 210
pages.recognize: Danfoss case and cold-room controller; E, A and S (status) codes.
pages.title: What Do Danfoss EKC 202 & AK-CC 210 Alarm Codes Mean? Full List
pages.h1: What do Danfoss EKC 202 and AK-CC 210 alarm codes mean?
pages.meta: Every Danfoss EKC 202 and AK-CC 210 code: E1, E6, E25-E29 faults, A1-A61 alarms and the S status codes that explain why the box isn't cooling right now.
pages.short_answer: Short answer: these controllers show three kinds of code. E-codes are faults — a sensor error or a defect in the controller. A-codes are alarms from daily operation — temperature, door, inputs, standby. S-codes are status messages that explain why nothing seems to be happening: refrigeration stopped by the main switch or the thermostat, a defrost in progress, a door open. The EKC 202 and the AK-CC 210 share most codes; the table marks which controller each one applies to.
pages.display_html: When there's an error the LEDs on the front flash and the alarm relay switches on. Push the top button to see the alarm report, and keep pushing to see any others. E-alarms appear the moment the error occurs; A-alarms only after their time delay has run out, and an A-alarm stays hidden while an E-alarm is active. Push the upper button briefly (1 second) to show the current status code.

table_rows.meaning: Real-time clock fault — check the battery and reset the clock
Maximum hold time (AK-CC 210: information that the time set in parameter o16 has expired)
Alarm signal from the DI1 input
Condenser alarm
Regulating
Waiting for the end of a coordinated defrost
Compressor ON-time
Compressor OFF-time
Drip-off time
Refrigeration stopped by the main switch
Refrigeration stopped by the thermostat
Defrost sequence — defrosting
Defrost sequence — fan delay
Refrigeration stopped because of an open DI input
Door open (open DI input)
Emergency cooling
Manual control of outputs
Case cleaning

diagnosis: Read every report. Push the top button to step through the alarm report. Fix E-codes first — an active E-alarm hides any A-alarm behind it.

If it's warm but not alarming, read the status code. A brief press of the upper button shows it: S10 means refrigeration was stopped by the main switch, S11 by the thermostat, S16 by an open DI input, S17 a door open; S14 and S15 are a defrost in progress.

A45 standby is urgent on an AK-CC 210. Refrigeration has been stopped via the r12 main switch or a DI input — and on the AK-CC 210 the alarm relay is not activated, so a remote alarm system won't call anyone.

Know which sensor is which. The EKC 202 uses an air sensor (Sair) and an evaporator/defrost sensor (S5). The AK-CC 210 uses S3 in the air flow before the evaporator, S4 after the evaporator, and S5 on the evaporator for defrost. Live readings are in the service menu (EKC 202: u09 = S5, u69 = Sair).

Replacement sensors must match. Pt1000 sensors are normal; PTC 1000 Ω or NTC 5,000 Ω (at 25 °C) sensors can be used instead, selected in parameter o06 — and all sensors on one controller must be the same type.
A60 is a food-safety record. It's the AK-CC 210's HACCP high-temperature alarm — log the actual product temperature when you see it.
E6 is the clock. Check the battery and reset the clock.

parts.part: Door switch on a DI input
Main switch setting r12, or a DI standby input
The controller and its clock battery

pages.name: Danfoss Optyma Plus
pages.recognize: Controller built into a Danfoss condensing unit; A2, A17, A80, A96.
pages.title: What Do Danfoss Optyma Plus Alarm Codes Mean? A2, A17, A80, A96
pages.h1: What do Danfoss Optyma Plus condensing unit alarm codes mean?
pages.meta: Every Danfoss Optyma Plus controller code: A2 LP, A17 HP, A45, A80 condenser blocked, A96 discharge temperature, A97, A98 and the E sensor errors, explained.
pages.short_answer: Short answer: the Optyma Plus controller is mounted on the condensing unit — the outdoor or machine-room half of the system — so its alarms are about protecting the compressor and condenser: low suction pressure (A2), a high/low pressure safety trip (A17), a blocked condenser (A80), too-high discharge temperature (A96), a safety input (A97) or the speed drive (A98). E-codes are controller, sensor and pressure-transmitter faults. Danfoss's full list is below.
pages.display_html: When there's an error the LEDs on the front flash and the alarm relay switches on; push the top button to see the alarm report. E-alarms show the moment the error occurs; A-alarms only once their time delay has passed, and an A-alarm stays hidden while an E-alarm is active.

table_rows.meaning: No refrigerant selected — set parameter o30
DI2 alarm — check the function that sends a signal to the DI2 input
Safety alarm — a safety function on DI2 or DI3 is activated; check that input and the compressor's direction of rotation
Drive alarm — alarm from the speed regulation; check the speed regulation
Error on pressure transmitter Pc (condensing pressure)
Error on the aux sensor (S5)
Error on the air (ambient) sensor S2
Error on the discharge sensor S3
Error on the suction gas sensor S4
Error on pressure transmitter Ps (suction pressure)

diagnosis: Push the top button and read the report. Note every code before resetting anything.
A45 isn't a failure. Standby means refrigeration was stopped via parameter r12 or the DI1 input; r12 and/or DI1 start it again.

A80 is the one you can act on. Airflow across the condenser has decreased, and Danfoss's action is simply: clean the condensing unit. The alarm is raised when condensing temperature stays too high — limit set by A70 — for the delay set by A71.

A2, A17 and A96 are protections — don't keep resetting them. Danfoss's instruction for all three is to follow the condensing unit's own instructions. The controller counts high- and low-pressure trips (read-outs P51 and P52): a climbing count points at a system problem, not a one-off.

Discharge temperature is handled in stages. If the discharge temperature (sensor Td) gets too high, the controller first reduces compressor capacity and runs the condenser fan at 100 %; if that doesn't bring it down it stops the compressor and raises A96, reconnecting the compressor once the temperature is 10 K below the limit.
Sensor and transmitter errors (E20, E30–E33, E39): check the sensor and its connection.
A11 means no refrigerant type has been selected — parameter o30 has to be set.
pages.extra_html: The compressor itself — how it works and why these protections exist — is general compressor theory, which our sister site aircompressorcodes.com covers. This page stays with what the Optyma Plus controller reports.

pages.name: Heatcraft intelliGen
pages.recognize: OLED display with a green / yellow / red light bar; AL, ER and IN codes.
pages.title: What Do Heatcraft intelliGen Codes Mean? AL01, ER01, IN01 & More
pages.h1: What do Heatcraft intelliGen (Bohn / Larkin) AL, ER and IN codes mean?
pages.meta: Every Heatcraft intelliGen code on Bohn and Larkin unit coolers: AL alarms, ER errors, IN information and A2L leak codes. What each means and what to check.
pages.short_answer: Short answer: intelliGen shows the code on the unit's OLED display and backs it with a light bar. Green is normal. An error (ER code) on any evaporator turns every light bar on the system yellow, with the unit that has the problem flashing yellow; an alarm (AL code) turns them all red, with the unit causing it flashing red. IN codes are information about conditions worth correcting, such as too many or too few defrosts.
pages.display_html: Before chasing a code, check the unit isn't in Service or Product Load mode — both pump the system down and switch off the expansion valve, fans and heaters, which looks exactly like a failure. The Monitor menu shows live sensor readings, and every board logs box temperature, coil temperature, suction pressure and temperature, superheat, valve steps, door switch and volts every minute for 60 days — the log copies to a USB drive for the technician.

table_rows.meaning: Spare I/O error
Auxiliary temperature probe error
Log disrupted — pull the data log to confirm missing data, then power cycle
Aux temp override — the aux temperature sensor was assigned to two functions; no action required
EV (evaporator) connection lost
High humidity
Low humidity
Humidity sensor error
LL connection lost — the three digits shown are the last 3 digits of the disconnected system's IP address
A2L sensor fault
A2L service (X = leak-detection sensor number)
A2L mitigation (X = leak-detection sensor number)
A2L refrigerant mismatch
A2L mitigation controller communication loss — check the RS-485 wiring and its polarity
LL high box temperature
LL low box temperature
Too few defrosts — 8 consecutive defrosts ended on time

diagnosis: Find the flashing unit. On a multi-evaporator system every light bar changes colour, but only the unit with the problem flashes — go to that one and read its display.
Rule out Service and Product Load mode (see above).

Sensor codes (ER01–ER04, AL04): compare before replacing. Read the suspect sensor in the Monitor menu and compare it with a thermometer at the same spot. Or test it in stirred ice water: at 32 °F it should read 32,650 Ω — more than about 1,000 Ω off, replace it. Sensors don't need to be removed from the evaporator for checking.

ER16 low superheat. intelliGen raises it when a board runs below the minimum superheat setting for 2 minutes. Check for an iced coil and the refrigerant type setting, then whether the expansion valve closes: pump the system down with the liquid-line valve closed, put the system in Service mode, reopen the liquid valve — if suction pressure rises, the valve is leaking.

Box won't reach temperature (AL01 with the system running): Heatcraft's own sequence is — system running? refrigerant charge, operating superheat, high superheat with the valve wide open, low-pressure switch, equipment capacity against the load, box setpoint, compressor, condenser coil dirt, non-condensables, condenser fan, refrigerant type setting, iced coil, defrost settings, superheat setpoint, and °F/°C display.

A2L units: AL12 and ER32–ER37 are leak-detection events. Units with A2L refrigerant carry a refrigerant detection system; when a leak reaches the mitigation level it takes over and the display shows AL12. Follow the unit's A2L safety instructions and call a technician.
ER19: replace the clock battery — a coin cell on the iRC board.
Pull the log. Errors and alarms are logged as they start and end (up to 500 entries) — copy them to USB so the technician sees the history, not just the current code.

parts.note: Factory intelliGen systems use the 300 psia transducer; the 139.7 psia setting is for Beacon II and QRC retrofits.
On a 208 V supply the transformer must be on the 208 V tap.

parts.part: iRC board, iRC user interface and ribbon cable

families: Beacon II Smart Controller (LCD display module)
pages.name: Heatcraft Beacon II
pages.recognize: Two-digit LED on the evaporator board (A1–A4, E1–E9); optional LCD Smart Controller.
pages.title: What Do Heatcraft Beacon II Codes Mean? A1-A4, E1-E9, *BOXHI
pages.h1: What do Heatcraft Beacon II (Bohn / Larkin) alarm and error codes mean?
pages.meta: Every Heatcraft Beacon II code: board alarms A1-A4, errors E1-E9 and Smart Controller messages like *BOXHI, *INFLT and +COMM+. Meaning, checks and fixes.
pages.short_answer: Short answer: Beacon II reports on the evaporator board's LED readout with A-codes (alarms about box conditions and start-up) and E-codes (sensor, superheat, compressor-safety and wiring errors). If the optional wall-mounted Smart Controller is fitted, it repeats alarms as text — *BOXHI, *INFLT, +COMM+ — shows "CALL FOR SERVICE" with the system number, and sounds a buzzer.
pages.display_html: What matters most is whether the system is still allowed to run. With a failed suction sensor, room sensor (on the master board) or pressure transducer, Beacon II pumps down and stays off until the fault is cleared. With an oil-pressure or high/low-pressure cutout it pumps down and retries three times, each after the 4-minute hold-off; after the fourth try the alarm contacts close and the alarm is displayed. Once the repair is done, clear it by cycling the system through SERVICE mode.

table_rows.meaning: Outdoor temperature sensor shorted
Board is locked — settings cannot be changed
Unlock the board settings
Box temperature too low
System start-up failure — the compressor pumps down and tries to restart after 4 minutes (not on QRC systems)
Power to the system was lost

diagnosis: Write down the code, the system number and whether the compressor is running before resetting anything.

Check sensors with the monitor button. It displays what the suction (SCt), defrost (dFt) and room sensors are reading — compare each against a thermometer at the same point. Or test in stirred ice water: 32,650 Ω at 32 °F; roughly 1,000 Ω higher or lower means replace the sensor. Don't remove sensors from the evaporators to check them.

E6 low superheat — Heatcraft's sequence: check the refrigerant type setting; check the coil for ice (defrost settings, defrost sensor, heater amps); check the board's valve step position; check that the expansion valve closes (pump down — does the low-pressure switch open?); check the compressor is actually running; compare the suction sensor with the real suction-line temperature and the transducer with gauges.

E7 compressor shut down — which safety? A low-pressure trip points at the refrigerant type, charge, the LPS setting (freezers: 0 psig cut-out, 10 psig cut-in), a stuck or blocked valve, an iced coil or line sizing. A high-pressure trip points at overcharge, non-condensables, the condenser fan motor or blade, a dirty condenser coil, head-pressure or fan-cycling controls, or a liquid-line restriction.
+COMM+ and E9 are wiring. The communication wiring runs MULTI OUT to MULTI IN between boards — never OUT to OUT or IN to IN.
LED not lit at all: check the disconnect, fuses and breakers, the transformer's primary and secondary voltage, and 24 V at the control board before replacing the board.
After service: at start-up the system may cycle off at 2 minutes with a low-superheat error a few times while the expansion valve finds its setting — Heatcraft's instruction is to let it run.

parts.part: Low- and high-pressure safety switches, compressor contactor and overloads
MULTI IN / MULTI OUT communication wiring
Evaporator transformer and 24 VAC board supply
parts.note: The first suspects when the board LED is not lit at all.

pages.name: Dixell XR06CX / XR60CX
pages.recognize: Small Dixell XR display on many Norlake and Kolpak boxes; P1, HA, LA, dA, CA.
pages.title: What Do Dixell XR06CX / XR60CX Codes Mean? P1, HA, LA, dA, CA
pages.h1: What do Dixell (Emerson) XR06CX and XR60CX alarm codes mean?
pages.meta: Every Dixell XR06CX / XR60CX code: P1-P4 probe failures, HA/LA, HA2/LA2, dA, EA, CA and the OF/PoF keypad lock. What it means and what the controller does.
pages.short_answer: Short answer: Dixell's XR controllers flash a short message on the display. P-codes are probe failures, HA/LA are high and low temperature alarms, HA2/LA2 are condenser temperature alarms (XR60CX with a condenser probe), dA is the door, EA an external alarm, and CA is the serious one — a critical input that switches every output off. OF (XR06CX) or PoF (XR60CX) just means the keypad is locked.
pages.display_html: How each alarm recovers is fixed by the manual. Probe alarms start a few seconds after a probe fails and stop a few seconds after it reads normally again. HA, LA, HA2 and LA2 stop as soon as the temperature is back to normal. EA and CA (serious-alarm mode) recover as soon as the digital input is released — but CA in pressure-switch mode (XR60CX) only recovers by switching the controller off and on. To unlock the keypad, hold the up and down keys together for more than 3 seconds until on (XR06CX) or Pon (XR60CX) appears.

values.P1: Compressor runs on a timer (Cy/Cn; Con/COF on XR60CX)

table_rows.meaning: Keypad unlocked
No alarm recorded
The selected probe is not enabled (in programming mode: no parameter present in Pr1)

diagnosis: Note the message and the actual box temperature. A probe alarm means the display itself can't be trusted.

P1 means the box is cooling on a timer. With the room probe failed, the compressor runs by time — on for Cy minutes, off for Cn (Con/COF on the XR60CX). With Cy at 0 the compressor stays off; with Cn at 0 it runs continuously. Check what yours is set to before assuming the box is safe.

P2 means defrost ends on time. With the evaporator probe failed, defrost stops at the maximum length (Md) instead of on temperature — so the coil can come out of defrost with ice left on it, or stay in defrost longer than it needs to.

Check connections before replacing a probe — Dixell's own instruction. Probes are NTC (XR06CX: up to two; XR60CX: up to four, NTC or PTC). The read-only parameters d1 and d2 (XR06CX) show what the thermostat and evaporator probes are reading.

Probe placement matters. Mount probes bulb-up so liquid can't get in; keep the thermostat probe out of air streams; put the defrost-termination probe among the evaporator fins in the coldest spot, where most ice forms and away from heaters — otherwise defrosts end early.
dA: with the door open, HA and LA are disabled. The door alarm comes on after the delay set in parameter di, and what the compressor and fans do while the door is open is set by parameter dC.

CA: find what's on the digital input. In serious-alarm mode (i1F = bAL) or pressure-switch mode (i1F = PAL) every output goes off. A tripped pressure switch is a refrigeration problem for a technician.

parts.part: Condenser coil (with a condenser probe fitted)
Door switch on the digital input
External alarm device or pressure switch on the digital input

pages.name: KE2 Evaporator Efficiency
pages.recognize: Scrolls alarms in plain words with a yellow or red LED beside the readout.
pages.title: What Do KE2 Evaporator Efficiency Alarms Mean? Full List & Fixes
pages.h1: What do KE2 Evaporator Efficiency (KE2 Evap) alarms mean?
pages.meta: Every KE2 Evaporator Efficiency alarm: HIGH/LOW AIR TEMP, LOW SUPERHEAT, PRESSURE SENSOR, T1-T4 SENSOR, DOOR SWITCH, EXCESS DEFROST. Meaning and fixes.
pages.short_answer: Short answer: the KE2 Evap scrolls its alarms in plain words, and the LED beside the readout tells you how serious it is. Yellow is an advisory alarm — the controller keeps running. Red is critical — the controller turns the system off to prevent compressor damage. If the auxiliary relay is set up as an alarm relay it switches too, and an internet-connected controller can e-mail or text the alarm.
pages.display_html: Every alarm has a matching entry in the VARIABLES menu with more information — room temperature, coil temperature, suction temperature and pressure, valve % open. KE2 also warns that many alarms are the result of incorrect wiring of the controller, sensors or valve, so every corrective action should include a wiring and installation check.

table_rows.meaning: INTRO displayed with all LEDs flashing — the controller isn't operational until it has been configured (KE2 bulletins N.1.1 / Q.1.3)
An alarm condition has been corrected; shown for about 10 minutes or until BACK is pressed
KE2 SmartAccess only: the controller couldn't send an alarm e-mail — check the e-mail server settings
KE2 SmartAccess only: site name or password not accepted (both are case-sensitive)
KE2 SmartAccess only: the controller has stopped communicating with KE2's server — check the local network and internet connection

diagnosis: Yellow or red? Yellow means you have time to diagnose with the system running; red means the system is off and product temperature is rising.
Open VARIABLES and read the value KE2 lists for that alarm.
Sensor alarms decode instantly: a sensor reading of −87 means it's open or not connected; 180 or higher means it's shorted.

Then measure it. Unplug the sensor and compare its resistance with KE2's table — about 2,000 Ω at 77 °F, 5,114 Ω at 32 °F, 12,110 Ω at −4 °F. If it has been extended, check the splice. If it still looks right, swap in a sensor that isn't alarming: if the controller can't read a known-good sensor either, the controller is the problem.

LOW SUPERHEAT usually means the compressor didn't start. KE2's most common cause is a low-pressure control that was never set in the field — it is the installer's job, not the factory's. If the alarm comes and goes, and especially if it shows up in the fall as outdoor temperatures drop, suspect this first.

HIGH SUPERHEAT (valve systems only) triggers when superheat has been 2 °F above setpoint for 90 minutes with the valve at least 95 % open — check suction pressure, the refrigerant setting and valve operation; the system may be short of refrigerant.
PRESSURE SENSOR (red, system off): check the connector position, 5 V DC between the black and red wires, and the signal on green; a transducer removed from the system should read about 0 psig.
No display at all isn't an alarm, but the controller isn't running: check incoming power, the voltage jumpers for your supply and the board fuse.

parts.note: KE2's curve (about 2,000 Ω at 77 °F) differs from Heatcraft's (10,000 Ω at 77 °F), so sensors aren't interchangeable between brands.

pages.name: Norlake programmable controller
pages.recognize: Four-line LCD panel with an ALARM button; alarms in full sentences.
pages.title: What Do Norlake Walk-In Controller Alarms Mean? All 22 Explained
pages.h1: What do Norlake programmable walk-in controller alarms mean?
pages.meta: All 22 alarms on Norlake's programmable walk-in control panel: DOOR AJAR, ROOM TEMP HIGH/LOW, AIR FLOW LOSS, SENSOR FAILURE, DRAIN PAN and more, explained.
pages.short_answer: Short answer: Norlake's programmable panel spells alarms out in plain English. The ALARM button glows red and a buzzer sounds; press ALARM once to silence the buzzer, press it again to see the first alarm screen, and keep pressing to step through each active alarm until "NO MORE ALARMS". Each screen shows the date and time, and some carry a hint — for example "AIR FLOW LOSS 1 — Check Blower, Belts".
pages.display_html: Read the status line on MENU 1 too: USING PROD SENSOR means the air temperature sensor has failed and the room is being held on the product sensor; SENSOR FAIL MODE means the air and product sensors have all failed and — if sensor-fail control is enabled — the unit is running on the fixed Cool On / Heat On times. Cooling continues in both cases, but on backup logic.

table_rows.meaning: Controller memory (EEPROM) failure
Air-flow alarm from the second air-flow input (AIRFL2)
Product temperature above the product high set point for longer than the alarm delay
Product temperature below the product low set point for longer than the alarm delay
Room relative humidity above the high RH set point for longer than the delay (humidity-controlled rooms)
Room relative humidity below the low RH set point for longer than the delay
Compressor 1 alarm input (C1 AL) is active — a high- or low-pressure safety has tripped
Compressor 2 alarm input (C2 AL) is active
High-limit humidistat alarm from the humidity alarm input (HUM AL); the alarm text itself carries a personal-safety warning
Drain alarm input (DRAIN) is active — PCO Medium controllers only
Water alarm input is active
Smoke alarm input (SMOKE) is active — PCO Medium controllers only
Product temperature sensor failure
Second product sensor below its low set point (rooms with two product sensors)
Second product sensor above its high set point
Second product sensor failed — or it's enabled with no sensor connected to the product 2 input

diagnosis: Silence, then read every screen. ALARM once for the buzzer, then step through all active alarms — more than one may be active.
Check the status line for USING PROD SENSOR or SENSOR FAIL MODE (above).

Most alarms come from digital inputs. Compressor 1 and 2 alarms, air flow 1 and 2, door, water, smoke, humidity and drain are all inputs, each configurable as normally open or normally closed; the alarm sounds when the input matches its "Active if" setting for longer than the delay. A wrongly configured or failed input device can raise an alarm even when the refrigeration is fine.
AIR FLOW LOSS: look at the blower first. The alarm screen itself says Check Blower, Belts.

Sensor failures: the standard air sensor is a 10k thermistor (10,000 Ω; a 1k RTD is optional), and the board's NTC inputs are 10 kΩ ±1 % at 25 °C. Sensor calibration offsets are under the AUX2 key — a sensor that reads slightly off can be offset, but a failed one must be replaced.

POWER RESTART is informational. If enabled it appears 10 seconds after power-up, and the room keeps running on its configuration. The separate power-failure alarm uses a battery switch to the right of the user terminal: top = test, centre = off, bottom = on.
Ring Back sets how many minutes the buzzer stays silent after an alarm is silenced — if it keeps coming back, the condition is still there.

parts.part: Evaporator blower, belts and air-flow switch

parts.note: Test it with the switch in the top position: the buzzer sounds if the battery is OK.
